403	    def verify(self, message: Any) -> bool:
404	        """Verify the embedded signature against the embedded public key.
405	
406	        Accepts ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str`` exactly like
407	        :func:`merkle_verify`, to which this call delegates; it returns
408	        ``True`` only for the message that was actually signed. The proof
409	        itself carries no message and cannot authenticate its own origin.
410	        """

414	def _signature_matches_key(signature: MerkleSignature, public_key: MerklePublicKey) -> bool:
415	    """Non-raising check mirroring the constraints enforced by ``to_bytes``."""
416	    try:
417	        w, height, chains = _signature_params(public_key)
418	        index = signature.index
419	        wots_signature = signature.wots_signature
420	        auth_path = signature.auth_path
421	    except (ValueError, AttributeError):
422	        return False
423	    if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int) or index < 0:
424	        return False
425	    if index >= (1 << height):
426	        return False
427	    if not _nodes_well_formed(wots_signature):
428	        return False
429	    if not _nodes_well_formed(auth_path):
430	        return False

432	        return False
433	    if len(auth_path) != height:
434	        return False

438	def _validate_batch_fields(public_key: Any, signatures: Any) -> None:
439	    """Enforce the :class:`MerkleBatchProof` field types and structure."""
440	    if not isinstance(public_key, MerklePublicKey):
441	        raise TypeError("public_key must be a MerklePublicKey")
442	    if not isinstance(signatures, tuple):
443	        raise TypeError("signatures must be a tuple of MerkleSignature")

445	        if not isinstance(signature, MerkleSignature):
446	            raise TypeError("every signature must be a MerkleSignature")

453	    if any(former >= latter for former, latter in zip(indices, indices[1:])):

460	
461	    The batch generalises :class:`MerkleProof`: every
462	    :class:`MerkleSignature` in ``signatures`` is constrained by the same
463	    :class:`MerklePublicKey`, so the whole batch travels as one
464	    self-contained object and verifies with :meth:`verify`. ``signatures``
465	    must be a non-empty tuple whose leaf indices are strictly increasing
466	    (hence unique). The batch stores no messages and is a pure
467	    serialisation container: it offers neither authentication nor
468	    encryption of the wrapper itself.
469	    """

471	    public_key: MerklePublicKey
472	    signatures: tuple[MerkleSignature, ...]
473	
474	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
475	        _validate_batch_fields(self.public_key, self.signatures)
476	
477	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
478	        """Serialise to the versioned v1 batch wire format as ``bytes``.
479	
480	        The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAMBAT\\0"``; one version byte
481	        (1); the public-key length as 4 big-endian bytes; the signature
482	        count as 2 big-endian bytes; the complete v1 encoding of the
483	        public key; then, in tuple order, each signature's length as 4
484	        big-endian bytes followed by its existing v1 encoding constrained
485	        by that key. Encoding is deterministic: the same batch always
486	        produces the same bytes. Fields corrupted by bypassing the frozen
487	        constructor raise ``TypeError``/``ValueError`` instead of
488	        producing a malformed encoding.
489	        """
490	        if not isinstance(self, MerkleBatchProof):
491	            raise TypeError("to_bytes must be called on a MerkleBatchProof")
492	        _validate_batch_fields(self.public_key, self.signatures)
493	        if len(self.signatures) > _MAX_BATCH_SIGNATURES:
494	            raise ValueError("the signature count does not fit in 2 bytes")
495	        key_bytes = self.public_key.to_bytes()
496	        parts = [
497	            _BATCH_PROOF_MAGIC,
498	            bytes((_BATCH_PROOF_VERSION,)),
499	            len(key_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big"),
500	            len(self.signatures).to_bytes(2, "big"),
501	            key_bytes,
502	        ]
503	        for signature in self.signatures:
504	            signature_bytes = signature.to_bytes(self.public_key)
505	            parts.append(len(signature_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big"))
506	            parts.append(signature_bytes)

509	    @classmethod
510	    def from_bytes(cls, data: Any) -> "MerkleBatchProof":
511	        """Parse ``to_bytes()`` output back into a :class:`MerkleBatchProof`.
512	
513	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
514	        ``TypeError``. The embedded public key is recovered first and then
515	        constrains every signature. A bad magic, an unknown version, a
516	        zero public-key length or signature count, a length field that is
517	        out of bounds, truncation, trailing data, an invalid nested
518	        encoding, a signature inconsistent with the key, or indices that
519	        are not strictly increasing raises ``ValueError`` and no
520	        half-valid object is returned.
521	        """
522	        if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
523	            raise TypeError("batch proof data must be bytes or bytearray")
524	        data = bytes(data)
525	        if len(data) < _BATCH_PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:
526	            raise ValueError("batch proof encoding is truncated")
527	        if data[:8] != _BATCH_PROOF_MAGIC:
528	            raise ValueError("bad batch proof magic")
529	        if data[8] != _BATCH_PROOF_VERSION:
530	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported batch proof version: {data[8]}")
531	        key_length = int.from_bytes(data[9:13], "big")
532	        signature_count = int.from_bytes(data[13:15], "big")
533	        if key_length == 0:
534	            raise ValueError("the public key length must not be zero")
535	        if signature_count == 0:
536	            raise ValueError("the signature count must not be zero")
537	        key_end = _BATCH_PROOF_HEADER_BYTES + key_length
538	        if key_end > len(data):
539	            raise ValueError("batch proof encoding is truncated")
540	        public_key = MerklePublicKey.from_bytes(data[_BATCH_PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:key_end])
541	        offset = key_end
542	        signatures = []
543	        for _ in range(signature_count):
544	            if offset + 4 > len(data):
545	                raise ValueError("batch proof encoding is truncated")
546	            signature_length = int.from_bytes(data[offset : offset + 4], "big")
547	            if signature_length == 0:
548	                raise ValueError("a signature length must not be zero")
549	            signature_end = offset + 4 + signature_length
550	            if signature_end > len(data):
551	                raise ValueError("batch proof encoding is truncated")
552	            signatures.append(
553	                MerkleSignature.from_bytes(data[offset + 4 : signature_end], public_key)
554	            )
555	            offset = signature_end
556	        if offset < len(data):
557	            raise ValueError("trailing data after the batch proof encoding")
558	        return cls(public_key=public_key, signatures=tuple(signatures))
559	
560	    def verify(self, messages: Any) -> bool:
561	        """Verify every embedded signature against the embedded public key.
562	
563	        ``messages`` must be a ``tuple`` of the same length as
564	        ``signatures``; each member accepts
565	        ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str`` exactly like :func:`merkle_verify`,
566	        to which every item delegates in tuple order. Returns ``True``
567	        only when every signature verifies against its message; a
568	        non-tuple argument, a count mismatch, an illegal message member or
569	        any verification failure returns ``False``.

571	        if not isinstance(messages, tuple):
572	            return False
573	        if len(messages) != len(self.signatures):
574	            return False
575	        return all(
576	            merkle_verify(message, signature, self.public_key)
577	            for message, signature in zip(messages, self.signatures)
578	        )

581	class MerkleSigner:
582	    """Thread-safe, in-process few-times signer over a Merkle tree of W-OTS keys.
583	
584	    Leaves are allocated in increasing order starting at 0; a leaf is consumed
585	    only by a successful :meth:`sign`, :meth:`sign_batch`,
586	    :meth:`sign_with_checkpoint`, :meth:`sign_batch_with_checkpoint`,
587	    :meth:`sign_multiproof_with_checkpoint`,
588	    :meth:`sign_with_auth_state`, :meth:`sign_batch_with_auth_state` or
589	    :meth:`sign_multiproof_with_auth_state`. Once
590	    every leaf is spent, further calls raise :class:`KeyExhaustedError`.
591	
592	    Leaves can also be proactively voided with :meth:`advance_to` (or
593	    atomically recorded with :meth:`advance_to_with_auth_state`): after a
594	    crash or whenever state is uncertain, a caller skips leaves that may
595	    already have been exposed so they can never be signed again. Voiding only
596	    moves ``next_index`` forward — it never changes the keys, and there is no
597	    public way to move it backwards.
598	    """
599	
600	    def __init__(
601	        self,
602	        *,
603	        height: int = 4,
604	        w: int = 4,
605	        token_bytes: Callable[[int], bytes] = secrets.token_bytes,
606	    ) -> None:
607	        w = _validate_w(w)
608	        height = _validate_height(height)
609	        private_keys = []
610	        leaves = []
611	        for _ in range(1 << height):
612	            wots_private, wots_public = wots_keygen(w=w, token_bytes=token_bytes)
613	            private_keys.append(wots_private)
614	            leaves.append(_leaf_hash(w, wots_public.elements))
615	        self._init_state(w, height, tuple(private_keys), leaves, 0)
616	
617	    def _init_state(
618	        self,
619	        w: int,
620	        height: int,
621	        private_keys: tuple[Any, ...],
622	        leaves: list[bytes],
623	        next_index: int,
624	    ) -> None:
625	        layers = [leaves]
626	        while len(layers[-1]) > 1:
627	            level = layers[-1]
628	            layers.append(
629	                [_node_hash(level[i], level[i + 1]) for i in range(0, len(level), 2)]
630	            )
631	        self._w = w
632	        self._height = height
633	        self._private_keys = private_keys
634	        self._layers = tuple(tuple(layer) for layer in layers)
635	        self._next_index = next_index
636	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
637	        self._public_key = MerklePublicKey(w=w, height=height, root=layers[-1][0])
638	
639	    @property
640	    def public_key(self) -> MerklePublicKey:
641	        """The Merkle public key committing to every leaf (read-only)."""
642	        return self._public_key
643	
644	    @property
645	    def next_index(self) -> int:
646	        """Index of the next leaf that has not been spent or voided (read-only).
647	
648	        Shares the signing lock, so the value is linearised with every
649	        :meth:`sign`, :meth:`sign_batch`, :meth:`advance_to` and
650	        :meth:`checkpoint`.
651	        """
652	        with self._lock:
653	            return self._next_index
654	
655	    @property
656	    def remaining(self) -> int:
657	        """Leaves still available for signing: ``public_key.leaf_count - next_index``.
658	
659	        Reads through the same lock as :attr:`next_index`; it is ``0`` once
660	        every leaf has been spent or voided.
661	        """
662	        with self._lock:
663	            return len(self._private_keys) - self._next_index
664	
665	    def _checkpoint_bytes(self, next_index: int | None = None) -> bytes:
666	        """Serialise the full signer state; the caller holds the lock.
667	
668	        ``next_index`` renders the checkpoint at a candidate index without
669	        touching ``self._next_index``; it defaults to the current index.
670	        """
671	        if next_index is None:
672	            next_index = self._next_index
673	        body = (
674	            _CHECKPOINT_MAGIC
675	            + bytes((_CHECKPOINT_VERSION, self._w, self._height))
676	            + next_index.to_bytes(2, "big")
677	            + (len(self._private_keys) * self._private_keys[0].length).to_bytes(
678	                4, "big"
679	            )
680	            + self._public_key.root
681	            + b"".join(
682	                element
683	                for private_key in self._private_keys
684	                for element in private_key.elements

689	    def checkpoint(self) -> bytes:
690	        """Serialise the full signer state (all private keys) to ``bytes``.
691	
692	        The v1 layout is: the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAMSCP\\0"``; one byte each
693	        for the version (1), ``w`` and ``height``; ``next_index`` as 2
694	        big-endian bytes; the total element count as 4 big-endian bytes
695	        (always ``2 ** height`` times the chain count for ``w``); the 32-byte
696	        Merkle root; every W-OTS private element in leaf-then-chain order
697	        (32 bytes each); and finally the SHA-256 of all preceding content.
698	
699	        The checkpoint shares the signing lock, so a concurrent snapshot
700	        reflects the state either immediately before or immediately after an
701	        in-flight :meth:`sign`, never part-way through one. The blob contains
702	        every private key in the clear and the trailing hash only detects
703	        accidental corruption — store it as a secret.
704	        """
705	        with self._lock:
706	            return self._checkpoint_bytes()

708	    @classmethod
709	    def from_checkpoint(cls, data: Any) -> "MerkleSigner":
710	        """Restore a signer from ``checkpoint()`` output without randomness.
711	
712	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
713	        ``TypeError``. A bad magic, version, length, ``w``, ``height``,
714	        ``next_index`` outside ``0 .. 2 ** height``, element count, checksum,
715	        or a Merkle root that does not match the one rebuilt from the private
716	        keys raises ``ValueError`` and no instance is returned. The restored
717	        signer has the same public key and resumes signing at the saved
718	        ``next_index``; a checkpoint taken after the last leaf was spent
719	        restores an exhausted signer.
720	        """
721	        if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
722	            raise TypeError("checkpoint data must be bytes or bytearray")
723	        data = bytes(data)
724	        header = _CHECKPOINT_HEADER_BYTES
725	        if len(data) < header + _CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES:
726	            raise ValueError("checkpoint is too short")
727	        body, checksum = data[:-_CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES], data[-_CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES:]
728	        if body[:8] != _CHECKPOINT_MAGIC:
729	            raise ValueError("bad checkpoint magic")
730	        if body[8] != _CHECKPOINT_VERSION:
731	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported checkpoint version: {body[8]}")
732	        w = _validate_w(body[9])
733	        height = _validate_height(body[10])
734	        next_index = int.from_bytes(body[11:13], "big")
735	        element_count = int.from_bytes(body[13:17], "big")
736	        root = body[17:header]
737	        if next_index > (1 << height):
738	            raise ValueError("next_index exceeds the leaf count")

740	        chains = l1 + l2
741	        if element_count != (1 << height) * chains:
742	            raise ValueError("element count does not match 2 ** height * chains")
743	        if len(body) != header + element_count * ELEMENT_BYTES:
744	            raise ValueError("checkpoint length does not match the element count")
745	        if hashlib.sha256(body).digest() != checksum:
746	            raise ValueError("checkpoint checksum mismatch")
747	        private_keys = []
748	        leaves = []
749	        offset = header
750	        for _ in range(1 << height):
751	            elements = tuple(
752	                body[offset + i * ELEMENT_BYTES : offset + (i + 1) * ELEMENT_BYTES]
753	                for i in range(chains)
754	            )
755	            offset += chains * ELEMENT_BYTES
756	            private_keys.append(WOTSPrivateKey(w=w, elements=elements))
757	            endpoints = tuple(_chain_walk(element, b - 1) for element in elements)
758	            leaves.append(_leaf_hash(w, endpoints))
759	        signer = cls.__new__(cls)
760	        signer._init_state(w, height, tuple(private_keys), leaves, next_index)
761	        if signer._public_key.root != root:
762	            raise ValueError("Merkle root rebuilt from the private keys does not match")

765	    def advance_to(self, next_index: Any) -> tuple[int, int]:

770	        can never be signed again, and the next :meth:`sign` uses the target
771	        leaf. Only the index moves — keys, public key and tree are unchanged,
772	        and there is deliberately no way to move the index backwards.
773	
774	        ``next_index`` must be a non-boolean integer in the closed interval
775	        ``[self.next_index, public_key.leaf_count]``; a boolean or any other
776	        type raises ``TypeError``, and a target below the current index or
777	        above the leaf count raises ``ValueError``. Returns
778	        ``(before, after)``: the next-leaf index before and after the call. An
779	        equal target succeeds, returns the same value twice and neither
780	        changes the state nor draws randomness. The call shares the signing
781	        lock with :meth:`sign`, :meth:`sign_batch` and :meth:`checkpoint`, so
782	        it linearises as one atomic jump. Advancing to the leaf count

786	        checkpoint format.
787	        """
788	        if isinstance(next_index, bool) or not isinstance(next_index, int):
789	            raise TypeError("next_index must be a non-boolean integer")
790	        with self._lock:
791	            before = self._next_index
792	            leaf_count = len(self._private_keys)
793	            if next_index < before or next_index > leaf_count:
794	                raise ValueError(
795	                    "next_index must be between the current index and the leaf count"
796	                )
797	            self._next_index = next_index
798	            return before, next_index

807	        next-leaf index before and after the jump, exactly what
808	        :meth:`advance_to` returns for the same target, and ``envelope`` is
809	        the ``bytes`` :func:`auth_state_wrap` v2 envelope over the
810	        post-advance v1 :meth:`checkpoint` bytes — byte-for-byte identical to

812	        ``scheme="merkle"`` with the given ``key`` and ``generation`` and the
813	        existing v2 field order and HMAC-SHA-256 tag. An equal target succeeds
814	        and, even though the state is unchanged, still returns an envelope
815	        authenticating that state.

817	        Every argument is validated before the index moves: ``next_index``
818	        must be a non-boolean integer in the closed interval
819	        ``[self.next_index, public_key.leaf_count]``; ``key`` is keyword-only
820	        and must be a non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray`` shared secret;
821	        ``generation`` is keyword-only and must be a non-boolean integer in
